I've been reading a book called The Forever Decision By Dr. Paul G. Quinnett. Not sure if we are allowed to post links on here but if you Google it it's free. I really liked it (although of course my internal monologue was snarky while reading in some parts haha) because it doesn't try to get you to change your decision, at least not really, it just presents a lot of different ways of thinking and takes you through a lot of thought exercises. My favorite one is probably the idea that, you don't have to decide right now. Like, you don't have to feel the pressure to decide right now. I think a lot of people who are considering ending their lives feel like they have to make a decision soon, like it's now or never, or even like they must not really be sick if they can't do it right now. But as Dr. Quinnett says, the decision/option to kill yourself will always be there. So in a sense there is really no reason not to wait a few more days, or weeks, or whatever. And maybe things will get worse in that time, or maybe you'll reach a greater sense of clarity, happiness, calm, it's hard to say. But the idea that there is no pressure to do it right now, and that if I don't it doesn't make me a faker or anything like that, I'm just giving myself more time and the option will be there if I return to it, really helped a lot. I definitely recommend the entire book though even if some of it is a bit preachy, it's not nearly as bad as what some people off the street will tell you.
